request.query: Jarvislabs announces GPU price change effective date, new hourly prices for H100 H200 B200 GPUs

results.title: Jarvislabs’ October rates raise the cost of an unchanged GPU workload | AI Infrastructure Analysis
results.author: Internal Editorial Team
highlights:
Published increases apply to new usage and new reserved plans, while existing committed nodes retain their contract price.

IE Internal Editorial Team October 30, 2026 · 1 min read

...

A training budget can change even when the model and machine stay the same. A price update needs to be evaluated against the number of paid hours a workload actually consumes, including time spent waiting or retrying.

Jarvislabs’ September 24 notice sets new rates from October 5 at 00:00 IST: H100 SXM moves from $2.69 to $3.49 per GPU-hour, H200 SXM from $3.99 to $4.59, and RTX PRO 6000 from $1.89 to $2.19. The figures are in US dollars, exclude tax and apply across regions. The company says existing committed nodes keep their contracted price. Jarvislabs rates effective October 5, 2026.

## Price changes are not performance changes

For an identical H100 workload, the listed hourly increase is approximately 29.7%. That arithmetic says nothing about whether a different GPU, provider or configuration would complete the same task more cheaply. Such a comparison needs measured runtime and the same quality requirement.

Jarvislabs attributes the update to memory-supply costs. That is the provider’s explanation, not an independently established industry-wide cause. It also says storage rates are unchanged and directs buyers to request new reserved-plan pricing, so the notice alone cannot price a reserved deployment.

The central takeaway

Apply the new rates to paid workload hours and contract exposure; compare alternatives by completed-job cost, not hourly price alone.

...

The immediate question is which jobs are exposed to the new rates and which remain covered by existing commitments. Over time, higher hourly charges may make utilisation improvements more valuable, but only if they reduce paid time without increasing failure or operational effort. Watch the actual completed-job cost, rather than assuming the lowest advertised GPU rate is the cheapest useful service.

results.title: Jarvislabs Alternative: zCLOUD vs Jarvislabs on Capacity, Network, Region Control and Cost to Completion
highlights:
Jarvislabs wins on cost to completion, the bill for finishing one job, for short H100 jobs. It lists the H100 at $3.49 per GPU per hour, below zCLOUD's $3.75.

...

1. Ordering limit: A team ordering from the Jarvislabs dashboard, without a sales call, gets up to eight GPUs per instance, a single rented server. Jarvislabs sells H100 clusters through its sales team.
2. Region: Data rules can require servers in a specific country, such as Taiwan or the US.
3. Rising rates: Jarvislabs raised its H100 on-demand rate by about 30%, from the $2.69 that price tracker CostBench recorded in August 2026 to $3.49 in October. A team now pays about $0.80 more per GPU per hour than an August budget assumed.

results.title: India GPU Cloud Price & Availability Index, Q3 2026 | IndiCompute Research
results.author: Presear Softwares Pvt. Ltd.
highlights:
Key takeaways

- The same H100 hour costs up to 3.7 times more depending on where you buy it: from ₹217.89 at JarvisLabs to about ₹797 per GPU-hour for AWS p5 in Mumbai.
- Spot capacity is the largest lever: E2E lists H100 spot at ₹70 per hour against ₹379.05 on-demand, an 82% discount.
- Single-GPU access is now the norm, including at hyperscalers, and published price data is often inconsistent, so insist on a dated rate card.

Coverage: 1 July to 30 September 2026 · Published 15 October 2026 · 10 providers tracked · Prices in INR per GPU-hour, excluding GST. Prepared by IndiCompute Research, Presear Softwares Pvt. Ltd.

...

- Price dispersion is wide. Published on-demand H100 prices ranged from ₹217.89 per hour at JarvisLabs to about ₹797 per GPU-hour for AWS p5 instances in the Mumbai region, with E2E Networks at ₹379.05 and Cyfuture AI at ₹329 in between.
- Spot capacity is the largest lever. E2E lists H100 spot at ₹70 per hour against ₹379.05 on-demand, an 82% discount. In AWS Mumbai, an observed p5.48xlarge spot price of about US$14.61 per hour compared with US$66.05 on-demand, a 78% discount.
- Single-GPU access is now the norm, including at hyperscalers. AWS listed a one-GPU p5.4xlarge H100 instance in Mumbai at US$8.256 per hour, which undercuts the common claim that hyperscalers only sell H100 in eight-GPU blocks.
- Published price data is inconsistent. Third-party guides quote E2E’s H100 at anything from US$1.80 per hour to ₹379.05, and Cyfuture’s at ₹219 or ₹329. Buyers comparing quotes should insist on a dated rate card and the exact instance configuration.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.
